title: Audio Management Unit — Removal
abstract: Removal of the audio management unit and its rack from the forward equipment area, with the connector handling that keeps the contact retention within limits on a rack that is opened often.

sections.purpose: This task removes the audio management unit, and where required its rack, from the forward equipment area so that the unit can be replaced or the rack can be changed.
sections.job_setup_note: The passenger address system must not be in use and the cabin crew must be told before the unit is disconnected, because every cabin call station will go dead. The unit is light but the connector shells are heavy and will hang on their contacts if the unit is withdrawn without support.
sections.procedure: 1. Tell the cabin crew that the interphone and passenger address will be unavailable. 2. Put the aircraft on ground power and confirm that no boarding announcement is in progress. 3. Open the access panel in zone 133 and gain access to the equipment rack. 4. Release the circuit breaker for the audio management unit and tag it. 5. Support the unit with one hand and release the front latch. 6. Withdraw the unit fifty millimetres and support the two connector shells before they take any load. CAUTION: DO NOT LET THE CONNECTOR SHELLS HANG ON THEIR CONTACTS. THE RETENTION WILL BE OUTSIDE LIMITS AFTERWARDS AND THE FAULT WILL BE INTERMITTENT. 7. Disconnect both shells and cap them. 8. Withdraw the unit fully and put it on a clean surface. 9. Where the rack is also to be removed, release the four attachment fasteners and keep the countersunk washers AES832388-10 with them. 10. Release the protective sleeve LN112642-3C at the feedthrough and withdraw the harness clear of the rack. 11. Remove the rack KE27719-48 and cover the mounting face. 12. Check the module 2922RC in the lower position for security while access is available.
sections.close_out: Cap both connector shells and cover the rack aperture. Record the contact retention of any shell that was found loose. Tell the cabin crew when the system will be available again, and do not leave the aircraft with the circuit breaker tag in place and no defect entry.

type_data.effectivity_note: SOLANO-30 and SOLANO-34 aircraft; step 9 applies only where the rack is being changed

safety_precautions: Tell the cabin crew before the system is disconnected.
Support the connector shells before they take load.
